parts.label: a
parts.display_text: Uranium-238 can decay radioactively and can react chemically with fluorine. Explain which part of the atom is responsible for each property.

answer.text: Radioactive decay involves an unstable nucleus. Chemical reactions involve the electron configuration, especially outer-shell electrons.

source.collection_label: Tim Kirk · Oxford 2003 · 1998 question reproductions
source.title: 1998 IB Physics questions reproduced in Tim Kirk's study guide

parts.label: b.i
parts.display_text: A deuteron (²₁H) reacts with magnesium-24 (²⁴₁₂Mg), producing a sodium nucleus and an alpha particle. Write the balanced nuclear equation.

answer.text: ²₁H + ²⁴₁₂Mg → ²²₁₁Na + ⁴₂He. Both total nucleon number (26) and proton number (13) are conserved.

source.collection_label: Tim Kirk · Oxford 2003 · 1998 question reproductions
source.title: 1998 IB Physics questions reproduced in Tim Kirk's study guide

parts.label: b.ii
parts.display_text: Explain why a positively charged deuteron needs a minimum kinetic energy to approach a positively charged magnesium nucleus closely.

answer.text: The electrostatic force is repulsive. Kinetic energy is converted into electric potential energy as the deuteron approaches, so sufficient initial kinetic energy is needed to reach a small separation.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A laser emits 350 mW of light of wavelength 640 nm. Calculate the number of photons emitted in 1.0 s. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.

answer.text: One photon has energy hc/λ = 3.11 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. The total emitted energy is Pt = 0.350 J. N = Ptλ/(hc) = 1.1 × 10¹⁸ photons.

sup-fd11d9964ff5b7a5-w2:b.i.hint: Keep a separate account of nucleon number and electric charge on both sides of the decay.
notes: In alpha decay A decreases by 4 and Z by 2. In beta-minus decay a neutron becomes a proton; in beta-plus decay a proton becomes a neutron, with the appropriate emitted leptons.
Gamma emission changes nuclear energy without changing A or Z. Beta decay shares energy with a neutrino or antineutrino, giving a continuous beta spectrum.

notes: Energy released is (mass_initial − mass_final)c². Equivalently, it is the increase in total binding energy, not simply the difference in binding energy per nucleon.
When given binding energy per nucleon, multiply by the nucleon number first. Keep atomic and nuclear masses consistent so electron masses cancel correctly.

ibd-90c7459b463b96a2-qB2:whole.text: For a head-on approach, the alpha particle’s kinetic energy becomes electric potential energy at its closest point. E = 5.0 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 8.0 × 10⁻¹³ J. Set E = k(2e)(79e)/r. Thus r = (8.99 × 10⁹ × 158 × (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)²)/(8.0 × 10⁻¹³) ≈ 4.6 × 10⁻¹⁴ m.
